title: MV Tale Of Vassya -  REMAKE - (DEMO available)

posts.author: kelarly
posts.body:
*update*
Game is complete!
Totally free to play
Here!
INTRODUCTION:
Tale of Vassya: A New Day
is an older game I spent half a decade creating on RPG Maker VX Ace, and completed back in 2021. Since then, the story and characters have always been on my mind, as I have always envisioned them a bit differently. As I became more proficient in RPG Maker MV and Adobe Photoshop, I began thinking about remaking Tale of Vassya with a grander vision.
I ported my RMVX Ace file into RPG Maker MV and began the process! It took a few... hundred... hours more than I imagined, but the game began really shaping up, and now I'm closing in on completing the REMAKE!
I mostly created this remake for myself and my love for these characters. It's very hard to envision a character's true image with 32x32 pixel sprites, so the chance to enhance their battler sprites in RMMV turned this experiment in to an entire game remake. The game will be totally FREE, as I've used assets and music from other Ips. Even though I've probably spent close to $100 on it myself, I just want people to play and enjoy my story.
*Note: Some of the images had to be re-sized smaller because they were too large to fit together with the VX Ace images.
DEMO:
I added a new DEMO for Tales of Vassya REMAKE, use the link below to download it. The demo contains about the first 2 hours of each story, plus some side content (could be around 4-6 hours of gametime total). Let me know what you all think!
DEMO LINK ver 1.01
​
CONTENT:
Here are some major upgrades and changes to the original game that really pop when I look at them this way:
- Re-Imagined backgrounds and visuals
- Increased Resolution and Mapping
- Re-Created all faces and sprites
- Enhanced battle visuals and battlers
- Boss battle balancing and visuals
- Soundtrack has been completely revisited, and most of the music has been changed out. Feels like a completely new game!
​
Here are some upgraded features and systems that were not as well designed in the original game:
- Charge Battle System:
I utilized the charge battle system to allow for more strategy and interactive battles.
- Weapon Switching system:
During battle, each character may use their turn to switch their current equipment, changing the type of damage they inflict like "slashing" or "piercing" type damage.
Enemies will be weak to certain damage types, allowing the player to take advantage of an enemy's weakness to certain damage types.
- Skill Balancing
I balanced a lot of the skills, gave new/different skills to characters that did not previously have them, and introduced ultimate skills for each weapon type.
- Various other upgrades and features!
SYNOPSIS:
Tale Of Vassya includes 2 separate campaigns, each with their own stories, characters, events and battles. Each of the two stories include around 15 hours of story and gameplay and at least another 5+ hours of optional content if you choose to continue on. There is a ton of content to find in each story line, and much of it works to expand on the story and the world. I was heavily inspired by the Game of Thrones series and the Final Fantasy series for this game, as you will quickly see.
STORY:
The world of Vassya has been at peace for almost a century. All of the diverse city-states live and trade together to maintain a healthy world economy. One fateful night, King Orick Maxwell II, the King of Capitol City, was found murdered in cold blood. The culprit, a man named Dmitry Juleon, is still at large somewhere in Vassya. After the first royal murder in over 100 years, the world of Vassya is very much unsettled, and tensions are beginning to rise between the cities. It is up to our two main characters, Damian and Maxwell, to figure out how to restore Vassya to its peaceful time, and find their purpose along the way.
CHARACTERS:
Damian Marquis:
- Damian is a young man who has lived in Capitol City his entire life, and yearns to see the outside world. As an acting member of The City Guard, he helps watch the city streets and keep crime at bay. His mother tragically died of a mysterious illness when he was young. After his mother, he is one of the last remaining descendants of the Rhegar Lineage. He yearns to leave Capitol City and see all that Vassya has to offer.
Orick Maxwell III:
- Everyone he knows personally calls him "Maxwell". After the night of his Father's murder, Maxwell's life turned dark. Formerly the heir to the throne and captain of The City Guard, Maxwell abandoned his duties and fled Capitol City. Now a loner, Maxwell is searching Vassya for a purpose and answers as to why his family was tragically taken from him.
Pearce Yashra:
- Most known as the Genius of Capitol City. He is a member of the city guard and good friends with Damian and Maxwell. Pearce spent his youth moving around Vassya from city to city, and getting to know some of the world leaders personally. Pearce relies on logic to make his decisions, and specializes in precise weapon types.
Urian Triphe:
- Personal guardian knight of The Royal Capitol Family. Urian is very disciplined, and finds working with young, adventurous-types quite frustrating. Urian is incredibly loyal to the crown even after the King is replaced. He partially blames himself for the King's murder as he left the city on a mission during the night of The Tragedy.
Dmitry Juleon:
- He has been named the murderer of King Orick Maxwell II and many others. He has gone into hiding since the murder, and his motivations are unknown. All questions surrounding the murder of the King lead back to Dmitry.
Kiara Juleon:
- She is a kind, young girl who seems to want to follow Maxwell on his journey. She seems to know something about Dmitry Juleon, but it is uncertain what she knows...
The Red Hooded Man:
- A mysterious hooded man, who seems to know Damian, and appears to have supernatural abilities. His motivations are currently unknown.
CONCLUSION:
I intend to complete the game and have it released for play very soon. I'm in the beta testing phase right now. This version of the game looks a lot closer to my original vision, and I’m quite happy with how it turned out. Here's another link to the DEMO version, which includes the first 2 hours of each story (4-6 hours of playtime total).
DEMO LINK ver 1.01
If you are curious and would like to check out the original game, the image below will direct you to the original game’s page:
RPG Maker VX Ace: Tale of Vassya
Thanks for your interest, and let me know what you think!
​

I'd like to try the demo but sound-effecting messages is big NO for me. No matter which game I happen upon to have this "feature" it

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
A review (sort of).  Some of my points will be referenced by mini snip shots, rather than trying to describe who was doing what, where.
I have played the demo up till the point that Damian is heading to West Street.
I might have gone on a bit longer, but I couldn't take any more of the sound effects for the messages.  I would strongly recommend that you make this optional, as it would be shame to have people quit before they even start.
I think this game has potential, and I note that it is only in Beta, but I think it might benefit from a rethink on a couple of points.
Perhaps make the initial battle tutorial optional? Most people playing don’t need to be told this.  Even if they do, the second tutorial is still telling the player to use items wisely, and that they can fight or escape.  Once would, I think, be enough.
I hardly ever had enough TP to use a skill. I only got enough if I attacked often enough or got hit.  I have no problem with TP not being carried over, but it is possible to start each battle with more than the rather miserable 5 that they seemed to have.  I think a random number between 11-18 works quite well.
I think it is helpful for the player to have some idea of what the percentage chance is for a skill to inflict a status effect.  How else can I make an informed decision about whether to risk using it or not?  Though perhaps all of them work 100%?  Again, it would be good to know that.
Not every player will have English as their first language. Item description for carrot : “May heal blindness or raise defense.” So does “may” mean that it randomly won’t do those things? It says that it is heal blindness OR raise defense. Do I get a choice? Or again, is it random which it does?  Same with apple “may” heal poison “or” confusion. My guess is that it will heal whichever status affliction you have, so that it’s dual purpose. But it’s not clear.
Save crystals. So can’t I save anywhere?  This element has been discussed on many threads and in general it is thought that players prefer to be able to save anywhere.  RL has its demands, and many players might have to leave the game quickly.
I liked the music, but I was a bit disappointed that you seem to be using all the default sound effects.  Even if you only changed the cursor sound that would make a big difference as it is used so much in the menus.
Spoiler:
Typos
There are quite a number of these, mostly punctuation, though there are also a couple of places with missing words.  The following are only examples, there were others.  You will need to proof read carefully.
Full stop/period after Well or make it a comma and then lower case H.
Should read "to be let outside the walls."
Full stop after ready.
Nope.  "Pearce and me".
Should read "inside the city walls".  The previous goblin dialogue had the same omission.
Wrong emote choice?
She appears to be smiling, which doesn't go with things being horrid.
I skipped on too fast to take a screen shot, but when the man who escorted Yuoran Triphe is thanked for his service, we get the Angry emote.
Overall, as I said at the beginning, I think this has potential, and I would encourage you to continue.  If I were to stress just one thing, it would be to make the message sound optional.  Too many players don't like it.

posts.author: woootbm
posts.body:
Heya, I played your game briefly and did an impressions video. You can watch it
here
if you are brave! There will be some overlap with some of the points made below, but there's value in hearing reactions to things in real time, too.
I apologize for forgetting that I've played one of your games on my channel before, I promise I'm not trying to harp on you.
As you know, I tend to be one of the harsher critics on here so steel yourself for what's to come.
Spoiler:
The review
Spoiler:
Positive notes
The pacing of the story is pretty good. Although there are some easy opportunities to trim some redundant segments (covered in the video). I also hope that things pick up again quickly after the point I stopped at.
Music choices were interesting.
It seems like there's some kind of conspiracy around the killer. This makes things interesting, I hope there's more here like the suspect is a patsy and Geddard is behind it or something.
The animated battle sprites are a nice touch.
Spoiler:
Neutral/suggestions
Is this game meant for kids? I kind of ask this during the video. To turn this into actionable feedback, I'd say either make that more apparent or give things a little more edge. It sometimes feels like I'm playing as Ned Flanders.
I hope the nepotism is supposed to show some sort of corruption or flaw with these characters. But I'm guessing it's not.
While the starting city is built in a way that the player will always find where to go, it would be better to give the player some kind of direction. Damian, presumably, knows this city so it makes no sense for him to have to find things.
I've seen some comments about the message sounds. My advice would be to find a sound with less attack (which means less clicky or poppy, in this case). And to reduce the frequency with how often the sound plays so it's farther away from playing on every character.
Enemies should fall over or disappear when defeated. Seems a little strange they just stay in a "taking damage" pose.
The stinger music at the end of combat feels like something at organist would play at a sports event (here in the States, anyway). Would suggest replacing something with a bit more instrumentation to match the rest of the music.
Spoiler:
Negative notes
The opening flashforward(?) is too disconnected to understand what it has to do with anything. It seems like the point of the scene is to tell the audience that Damian is a capable dude. It would be better to show this somehow.
Damian is just staring at the walls when the plot shows up at his door. This doesn't make him seem like an interesting or capable guy.
The "Identify" skill is wildly useless in this opening.
There's nothing really interesting about this combat. Although these seem to be temporary characters so hopefully this opens up outside the tutorial/intro area.

Oh Hey Wootbm thanks! I am subscribed to your youtube, but I didn't notice my game as in one of your vids. I am brave, and I understand where your criticisms come from, so I'll definitely give it a watch.
The story is most important to me, and I'm not sure how far you got into the demo itself, but here is some extra info in case it interests you any more than in your playthrough:
- I wouldn't say the story is for kids at all. I wanted to show how optimistic the characters are during the prologue, and then after the murders and the time skip, the story is much more serious, especially in Maxwell's story.
- The opening is a flashback to Damian's mother and her expedition, which is an important turning point in history before the current day. There's a lot more connections and additional flashbacks to that event in the first few hours of the game.
- It's definitely a slow start to the story, and it picks up quickly after the prologue. There is a lot of mystery surrounding the murder and why it happened the way it did.
Anyway, thanks again for playing! And I'll check out your video for sure!

Hey thanks very much for playing! I'm glad you enjoyed it.
The final game includes about 15 hours for each story, so about 30 hours for both.
I liked writing the notes left behind by past characters. The more notes that you gather, the more they reveal about the past events that shaped the present day happenings. The final game has about 60 notes, spanned between the two main stories.
The game is complete right now. I'm working on testing and balancing everything. I also wanted to add hints and helpful language to assist players in knowing where they should go next. It's a long game with a lot of dialogue, so I can see people missing where they are explained where to go next.
I'm hoping to have the game released soon, though I work full time and have children, so the time I have to work on rpg maker is getting smaller and smaller every day

posts.author: Sword_of_Dusk
posts.body:
Gave this a shot, but only put in 45 minutes. Find my thoughts in the spoiler tag below.
Spoiler:
Observations
- First up, are so many people meant to be related? Multiple people share a surname, but then some seemingly have no relation to each other based on the dialogue. It's a bit strange, especially if lineages are shared too widely.
- You have a lot of weird pauses in dialogue that can't be skipped past. That's unnecessary and slows down the pace.
- I can tell you aren't a native English speaker (or so it would seem). The script could use a pass by someone more fluent. There's a lot of dialogue that reads oddly.
- The tutorial fights are mindless. You aren't required to do anything but hit Attack. It would be a good idea to at least make the Goblins a group of two to better match your party of three.
- I can tell you're trying to make Dmitry feel threatening, but he falls incredibly flat. He has nothing to say whatsoever, which isn't a problem in and of itself, but you fail to use his actions to get across how dangerous he is. I honestly fail to believe he slew a whole bunch of soldiers so easily when the city guard seemed to have little trouble leading him into a corner. Then you battle him, and he's nothing. He even runs from you!
He would come off better if he dealt the party a heavy blow to end the battle and then ran, as then it would appear like he just grew tired of dealing with them and wanted them out of his way.

Spoiler:
Observations
- First up, are so many people meant to be related? Multiple people share a surname, but then some seemingly have no relation to each other based on the dialogue. It's a bit strange, especially if lineages are shared too widely.
- You have a lot of weird pauses in dialogue that can't be skipped past. That's unnecessary and slows down the pace.
- I can tell you aren't a native English speaker (or so it would seem). The script could use a pass by someone more fluent. There's a lot of dialogue that reads oddly.
- The tutorial fights are mindless. You aren't required to do anything but hit Attack. It would be a good idea to at least make the Goblins a group of two to better match your party of three.
- I can tell you're trying to make Dmitry feel threatening, but he falls incredibly flat. He has nothing to say whatsoever, which isn't a problem in and of itself, but you fail to use his actions to get across how dangerous he is. I honestly fail to believe he slew a whole bunch of soldiers so easily when the city guard seemed to have little trouble leading him into a corner. Then you battle him, and he's nothing. He even runs from you!
He would come off better if he dealt the party a heavy blow to end the battle and then ran, as then it would appear like he just grew tired of dealing with them and wanted them out of his way.
Click to expand...
Thanks for taking time to play the demo.
I actually took some of your advice and spiced up the prologue section a bit. I also changed up the battle with Dmitry to be closer to how you described. I think it does show him to be more of a threat.
I appreciate your feedback, and I think these changes are going to help make the prologue a bit more interesting.
